verses.1: Gazing at Mahodara killed by Sugriva, mighty Mahaparsva's eyes turned red in anger. He created a commotion in the army of Angada.
verses.2: That leader (Mahaparsva) severed the heads of Vanara leaders from their body just as wind drops fruits from stalks.
verses.3: Then with his arrows, that Rakshasa (Mahaparsva) shattered the arms of some, shoulders of some, sides, and ribs of some Vanaras.
verses.4: By the rain of arrows of Mahaparsva, the Vanaras were dejected and wore a sad look on their face and lost senses.
verses.5: Observing the army oppressed by the Rakshasa leader, Angada, endowed with broad shoulders, exhibited his might speedily like the ocean on full moon days.
verses.6: The foremost of the Vanaras (Angada), taking an iron bar flung on Mahaparsva in the battlefield.
verses.7: By that hit, Mahaparsva became unconscious and fell on the ground, senseless, from the chariot along with the charioteer.
verses.8: Jambavantha, the mighty king of Bears, rushed from his army that looked like a dark cloud. The great hero with his army resembling a heap of black mountain, in his fury seized a huge rock resembling a mountain peak, crushed the chariot and struck the horses.
verses.9: Jambavantha, the mighty king of Bears, rushed from his army that looked like a dark cloud. The great hero with his army resembling a heap of black mountain, in his fury seized a huge rock resembling a mountain peak, crushed the chariot and struck the horses.
verses.10: In a short while, regaining consciousness, mighty Mahaparsva struck Angada again with many shafts.
verses.11: Mahaparsva pierced three shafts into the chest of Jambavantha and attacked Gavaksha with many arrows.
verses.12: Seeing Gavaksha and Jambavantha afflicted by shafts, deluded with anger, Angada took hold of a dreadful iron bar.
verses.13: Vali's son Angada got enraged, seized an iron bar which shone like the radiant sun's rays and stood at a distance to kill Mahaparsva. Angada whirling the iron bar round and round hurled it around and thrown at Mahaparsva.
verses.14: Vali's son Angada got enraged, seized an iron bar which shone like the radiant sun's rays and stood at a distance to kill Mahaparsva. Angada whirling the iron bar round and round hurled it around and thrown at Mahaparsva.
verses.15: That iron bar hurled by Angada hit the forehead of the Rakshasa.
verses.16: Courageous son of Vali, enraged, with all speed, slapped the Rakshasa's ear adorned with shining earrings, with his palm.
verses.17: Angry Mahaparsva, who was endowed with speed and shining brightly, took hold of an extraordinary battle axe in one hand.
verses.18: Extremely enraged Rakshasa, hurled at Vali's son that axe that was cleansed with oil, the clean strong axe that was like feet of a mountain.
verses.19: Angada, full of fury, escaped Mahaparsva's aim to strike his left shoulder blade in violence.
verses.20: Angada, who was equal to his father in his prowess, was highly furious and himself clenched his fist which resembled thunderbolt.
verses.21: Angada who knew the vital parts, pierced into the middle of the breasts of the Rakshasa into the heart by his fist which was equal to Indra's thunderbolt.
verses.22: In that great conflict, struck by the fist, the Rakshasa (Mahaparsva's) heart broke and killed and fell on the ground.
verses.23: Mahaparsva having fallen down in the battle, the army was bewildered, and Ravana was overcome with anger.
verses.24: Highly rejoiced Vanaras roared in high pitch sound. The tall attics and gates of Lanka vibrated with sound. Even the gods, accompanied by Indra, made great sounds.
verses.25: Highly rejoiced Vanaras roared in high pitch sound. The tall attics and gates of Lanka vibrated with sound. Even the gods, accompanied by Indra, made great sounds.
verses.26: Hearing that great roar of the dwellers of heaven and of the forest-dwelling monkeys, the lord of rakshasas, the enemy of Indra, wrathfully took his stand facing the battle once more.
